The first run follows the procedure described in Section 4, using 10 random initial points, while the second run uses initial points collected from training on the small systems following the initialization algorithm described in Section E. The performance of these two approaches is compared in Fig. 11. While the ‘coldstart’ approach that uses random initialization continues to find better and better protocols as training goes on, the rate of improvement is low, reaching only F = 22% after 500 iterations. The transfer approach performs much better, reaching fidelities as high as F = 75%. While the optimized protocol for the N = 2 system is not directly applicable to the larger system (F = 13%), the qualitative strategy does not change. Fig. 12 compares the evolution of the density profile for the optimized protocol in the two system sizes. The optimization performance was boosted massively by utilizing knowledge of the smaller system. This extends a previous report of efficient scaling in the system size [20] to a case featuring different model parameters (U and α) and a different target state.
